paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's Word isn't a fence, it's a feast. The writer starts by saying, "Blessed are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the Law of the LORD" (Psalm 119:1). Then he says he rejoices in God's testimonies "as much as in all riches" (Psalm 119:14). This man is not gritting his teeth through a rulebook. He's DELIGHTED.

Now notice what he does about it. He doesn't brag, he prays. "Oh, that my ways were committed to keeping Your statutes!" (Psalm 119:5). "Teach me Your statutes" (Psalm 119:12). "Open my eyes that I may see wondrous things from Your law" (Psalm 119:18). I think he knows he can't do this on his own, and that's good news for you and me. The same God who gave the Word is the One who helps us understand it.

And it holds up when life gets loud. "How can a young man keep his way pure? By guarding it according to Your word" (Psalm 119:9), and "I have hidden Your word in my heart that I might not sin against You" (Psalm 119:11). So when the slander comes, he doesn't hit back. He "meditates on Your statutes" (Psalm 119:23). So take it from a stamper who got pulled out of a junk drawer: stay in the Word, baker, because it's your delight and your counselor (Psalm 119:24). And this psalm is NOT finished, so keep those ovens warm.
